title: Tensor addition of framed Cartier pairs before applying Kummer
statement:
Let $T$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $D_1,D_2\hookrightarrow T$ be effective Cartier divisors with ideals $\mathcal I_1,\mathcal I_2$ and dual line bundles $L_a=\mathcal I_a^\vee=\mathcal O_T(D_a)$ [def-pc-divisor-line-bundle], and let $s_a$ be the section of $L_a$ obtained by transposing $\mathcal I_a\hookrightarrow\mathcal O_T$. Put $W_a=T-|D_a|$ and $W=W_1\cap W_2$, and let $Z\hookrightarrow T$ be the closed subscheme with ideal $\mathcal I_1\mathcal I_2$ [def-weil-closed-immersion, def-weil-open-immersion]. Then $Z$ is an effective Cartier divisor with support $|D_1|\cup|D_2|$, and multiplication of ideals induces an isomorphism of framed pairs
$$(\mathcal O_T(Z),s_Z)\cong(L_1\otimes_{\mathcal O_T}L_2,s_1\otimes s_2).$$
Consequently their frame torsors with the specified sections over $W$ [lem-sc-line-bundle-torsor, def-amb-torsor-with-section] are identified by contracted product [def-sc-contracted-product-presentation]. Write $\alpha(P,s)\in H^1(T,W;\mathbf G_m)$ for the Ext-normalized relative torsor class [lem-amb-relative-torsor-cohomology, def-amb-relative-etale-cohomology]. Then
$$\alpha(P_Z,s_Z|_W)=r_1\alpha(P_{D_1},s_1|_{W_1})+r_2\alpha(P_{D_2},s_2|_{W_2}),$$
where $r_a$ is the enlargement-of-support map induced by the signed-cone map $(x,y)\mapsto(x,y|_W)$. Under the relative extension realization [lem-sp-relative-torsor-extension], this is the same equality of degree-one Yoneda classes
$$\beta_Z=q_1^*\beta_{D_1}+q_2^*\beta_{D_2}\quad\text{in }\operatorname{Ext}^1_T(i_{Z,*}\mathbf Z_Z,\mathbf G_m),$$
where $q_a:i_{Z,*}\mathbf Z_Z\to i_{D_a,*}\mathbf Z_{D_a}$ is the canonical restriction of supported constant sheaves. The sum is Baer addition. Each $r_a$ commutes with relative connecting homomorphisms for every short exact sequence of abelian coefficient sheaves, with the induced map on the other terms, and with coefficient maps. No smoothness, reducedness or proper-intersection assumption on the divisors is required; the local equation of $Z$ is $f_1f_2$.

proof.text: Work on a common affine refinement using exists_affineOpens_isRegularPrincipal and the existing mul_effectiveCartier theorem. The support_mul theorem and support_ker identify the support with the union, and ideal_mul gives the principal product equation. Construct the multiplication morphism globally: the tensor-bilinear universal property and local membership in the product ideal show that multiplication into O_T is killed by the product-ideal quotient, so the kernel universal property factors it through the product ideal. On the common affine refinement it sends the tensor of the two ideal generators to their product. The existing local free-generator isomorphism criterion proves that this morphism is an isomorphism. This constructs the global multiplication isomorphism without choosing incompatible local inverses.

source.place: Tags 01WT and 01WU, definition-sum-effective-Cartier-divisors and lemma-sum-effective-Cartier-divisors; explicit local proof

proof.text: Tensor the two dual evaluation isomorphisms and reorder the factors using tensor-mu to obtain an isomorphism from (I_1 tensor I_2) tensor (I_1-dual tensor I_2-dual) to O_T. Compare this with evaluation for the product ideal after the multiplication isomorphism from step 1. Tensoring by I_1 tensor I_2 is an equivalence because it is invertible; its full faithfulness lifts this comparison to the required dual isomorphism and gives exactly the stated evaluation equation. Directly unfold the transpose section through the unit-Hom equivalence to prove its evaluation identity. Tensor the two evaluation identities and use tensor right unitality. Full faithfulness of tensoring by I_1 tensor I_2 and cancellation of the evaluation isomorphism then prove the section equation. These are global identities, valid also on the empty scheme and in the presence of nilpotents.

source.place: Clause (b), product local equation; explicit dual-basis verification of the framed isomorphism

proof.text: Construct the canonical complement frames by cartierDivisorSectionPullback_isIso. Tensor the underlying ordinary-pullback frames via tensorPullbackFrames and transport by the inverse framed ideal-dual isomorphism of step 2. Monoidal pullback composition proves naturality, and the scalar formulas prove equivariance in both inputs. The antidiagonal invariance follows by adding the two translations. The general binary torsor quotient theorem gives the requested universal property by local torsor triviality and sheaf gluing. Pullback of the section identity from step 2 proves that the restricted canonical sections map to the product section.

proof.text: Apply relativeTorsorEquiv_add_of_equivariant to the tensor pairing and the two restricted specified sections. The theorem presents both torsors in the same injective resolution and adds their global cocycles and open lifts; the signed cone cycle (iCycles(t),-b) adds exactly. For support restriction use the cocycle-coordinate map formula: take the identity on the global complex, the section restriction on the open complex, and zero correction. Its global difference is zero and its open difference vanishes by naturality of the torsor-presentation isomorphism. Negation of the resulting raw-class equality gives the Ext-normalized formula.

source.place: Tag 03AJ, lemma-torsors-h1, injective lifting-torsor paragraph; agent-written relative addition calculation

proof.text: For W contained in V, restriction from the terminal object factors through V. Presheaf functoriality and uniqueness of terminal arrows give the section restriction square degreewise; extendMap preserves it. The actual shifted-cone arrow map therefore gives precisely the specified restriction. For every coefficient-complex map f, functoriality of homotopyCofiber.mapArrowHom, identity on the global term, and naturality of f on the open term give a commuting square of relative complexes. Passing to homology proves the first naturality clause. For the remaining relative class calculation of step 4, the restriction map keeps the global cocycle and restricts the chosen open lift; the actual-cone coordinates are (iCycles(t),-b), so this is exactly the signed-cone map required there.

proof.text: Identify a CartierPoleBoundarySpec representative with the canonical framed torsor extension. Its chosen canonical section equals the supplied section by injectivity of the frame-value map. The equivariant map to the representative extension lies over the supported section one: naturality of the constant-sheaf map identifies its restrictions, and the specified section maps to zero by the pole-boundary condition. The uniqueness clause for relativeExtension therefore identifies the pole-boundary class with the extension assigned to the framed torsor.

proof.text: Use relativeExtensionSupportMap_existsUnique for each containment of complements, obtaining exactly the supported constant restriction maps required by the statement. The relative_extension_enlarge theorem identifies precomposition with these maps with restriction of the specified section and with the actual signed-cone restriction map.

proof.text: Apply the injective additive relativeExtensionComparison at the product support. The normalization theorem sends each relativeExtension to minus the raw relative torsor class. Naturality under enlargement converts the pullbacks of the input extension classes to the two restrictions in step 4. That equality proves addition in derived Ext. Finally cartierPairYonedaClass is the additive inverse Yoneda-derived comparison applied to the negative class, so neg_add and map_add give the displayed equality of Yoneda classes, with its Baer group law. This reuses the existing normalization theorem instead of reconstructing Baer representatives.

source.place: Tag 010L, lemma-baer-sum and the immediately preceding construction; sites-cohomology.tex Tag 03AJ, fibre over one

proof.text: The naturality statement already supplies degreewise splittings of the coefficient complex row. Apply the existing relativeShortComplex_shortExact theorem at V and W to get the two short exact relative rows. The restriction maps on their three objects form a morphism of short complexes by the commuting coefficient-complex squares proved in step 5. Apply HomologicalComplex.HomologySequence.delta-naturality to this morphism, in every integer degree, to obtain the asserted connecting-map square. No fresh horseshoe resolution, augmentation-preserving lift, or enough-injectives choice is needed for this statement.
